Further elimination types. Write prem_y(f,g) for the remainder obtained by
pseudo-division in y, so that lc_y(g)^k f = h g + prem_y(f,g) for some
polynomial h and integer k >= 0. A common zero of f and g is a zero of
this remainder, also when the leading coefficient vanishes at the
specialization. Primitive parts below have integer coefficients with
gcd 1 and positive leading coefficient. In the two new types, only
powers of eta and T, and in the regular branch of type (VI) also powers
of eta-zeta_1 and of the numerators of L_1 and L_2, are removed when
they divide the polynomials under consideration; these factors do not
vanish on the respective branches.

Type (V): two values theta_1 = 4 and theta_2 = 2, taken by three and four
nodes, with A_0 = 1, so e = 6 and T = eta-21. Put
    pi_1(v) = v^3-b_1 v^2+b_2 v-b_3,
    pi_2(v) = v^4+c_1 v^3+c_2 v^2+c_3 v+c_4.
The first relation of (A9) gives b_3, with coefficient -T, M_1, M_2 and
M_3 give c_1, c_2 and c_3 with coefficients -2, -4 and -6, and the
second relation of (A9) gives c_4 with coefficient -T. All these pivots
are nonzero. The primitive numerator N_0 of M_4 is quadratic in b_2,
with leading coefficient 384 T^2. Let F_1 and F_2 be the primitive
numerators of M_5 and M_6, and let their primitive pseudo-remainders
modulo N_0 in b_2 be
    R_1 = r_1 b_2+r_0,   R_2 = r_3 b_2+r_2.
A solution annuls
    U = r_1 r_2-r_0 r_3,
    V_1 = Res_{b_2}(N_0,R_1),   V_2 = Res_{b_2}(N_0,R_2).
After removing the indicated nonzero factors and taking primitive parts,
it therefore annuls both Res_{b_1}(U,V_1) and Res_{b_1}(U,V_2).
Their primitive gcd Lambda is the elimination polynomial used here.
No r_i is divided out; a vanishing coefficient or identically vanishing
specialized remainder is included by these polynomial implications.

Type (VI): one node zeta_1 of value 6, one pair of value 4 and one class
of three nodes of value 2, with A_0 = 1, so e = 5 and T = eta-21. Put
    pi_1(v) = v^2-b_1 v+b_2,
    pi_2(v) = v^3+c_1 v^2+c_2 v+c_3.
The two sums, with L_0 = 1/(eta-zeta_1), give
    L_1 = [T zeta_1-(T+4)eta]/[2eta(eta-zeta_1)],
    L_2 = [(T+2)eta-T zeta_1]/[2eta(eta-zeta_1)].
If L_1 L_2 != 0, the relation pi_1'(eta) = L_1 pi_1(eta) gives b_2
with coefficient -L_1, M_1 and M_2 give c_1 and c_2 with coefficients
-2 and -4, and pi_2'(eta) = L_2 pi_2(eta) gives c_3 with coefficient
-L_2. Let N_0, F_1 and F_2 be the primitive numerators of M_3, M_4 and
M_5, whose degrees in b_1 are 3, 4 and 4. Form
    U = Res_{b_1}(N_0,F_1),   V = Res_{b_1}(N_0,F_2),
    Q_1 = prem_{b_1}(F_1,N_0),   Q_2 = prem_{b_1}(F_2,N_0),
    R = prem_{b_1}(N_0,Q_1),   W = Res_{b_1}(Q_2,R),
taking primitive parts and removing the indicated nonzero factors after
each operation. The degrees of Q_1, Q_2 and R in b_1 are 2, 2 and 1.
A solution annuls U, V and W, and hence both H = Res_{zeta_1}(U,V) and
J = Res_{zeta_1}(U,W). Let Lambda be their primitive gcd after removing
powers of eta and T. No coefficient of a pseudo-remainder is a pivot:
the construction uses polynomial operations throughout, so possible
specialized degree drops introduce no omitted branch.

If L_1 = 0, then zeta_1 = eta(1+4/T), b_1 = 2eta and L_2 = -L_0 != 0.
M_1 and M_2 give c_1 and c_2 and the logarithmic relation for pi_2 gives
c_3, leaving b_2 as the variable. The numerators of M_3, M_4 and M_5
have degrees 1, 2 and 2 in b_2. The resultants of the first with the
other two have degrees 16 and 18 in eta, and primitive gcd T^4.
If L_2 = 0, then zeta_1 = eta(1+2/T) and L_1 = -L_0 != 0. The
logarithmic relation for pi_1 gives b_2, M_1 gives c_1, pi_2'(eta) = 0
gives c_2 with coefficient 1, and M_3 gives c_3 with coefficient -6.
The numerators of M_2, M_4 and M_5 have degrees 2, 4 and 5 in b_1;
the resultants of the first with the other two have degrees 24 and 30,
and primitive gcd T^8. Thus neither zero branch is possible. Both L_i
cannot vanish together, since L_0 != 0.

Patterns for d = 21. There are 103 patterns (A_0; mu_1, ...) with e >= 2.
The preceding lemmas exclude all except the following 29:
    (1; 4, 4, 2), (1; 3, 3, 3, 1), (1; 3, 3, 2, 2);
    (1; 6, 2, 1, 1), (1; 5, 3, 1, 1), (1; 5, 2, 2, 1),
    (3; 5, 2, 1, 1), (3; 4, 3, 1, 1), (3; 4, 2, 2, 1),
    (3; 3, 3, 2, 1), (5; 4, 2, 1, 1), (5; 3, 2, 2, 1),
    (7; 3, 2, 1, 1);
    (1; 4, 2, 2, 1, 1), (1; 3, 3, 2, 1, 1),
    (3; 3, 3, 1, 1, 1), (3; 3, 2, 2, 1, 1),
    (5; 2, 2, 2, 1, 1), (7; 2, 2, 1, 1, 1);
    (1; 4, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1), (1; 3, 3, 1, 1, 1, 1),
    (1; 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1), (1; 2, 2, 2, 2, 1, 1),
    (3; 3, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1), (3; 2, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1),
    (5; 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1);
    (1; 2, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1), (3; 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1);
    (1; 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1).
For each of the first two patterns the exceptional node is
eta(1-4/T), with T = eta-21. The moments give respectively
pi'(eta) = 3 P_4(eta)/(128 T^2) and 7 P_6(eta)/(48 T^3), where
    P_4(23+m) = 382640+342880m+75528m^2+4760m^3+91m^4,
    P_6(23+m) = 4537920+6105600m+2794320m^2+479680m^3
                 +35724m^4+1200m^5+15m^6.
Both are positive for m >= 0, a contradiction. For (1;3,3,2,2),
the two-pairs discriminant is -4*6*4*K, where
    K = 3 P_K(eta)/(eta-1)^2,
    P_K(23+m) = 153072+204592m+57392m^2+3892m^3+77m^4 > 0.
Thus this case too is excluded for every real n >= 1.

The ten remaining patterns with e = 3 and the two patterns
(1;4,2,1,1,1,1), (3;3,2,1,1,1,1) are of type (II). The three patterns
(1;4,2,2,1,1), (1;3,3,2,1,1), (3;3,2,2,1,1) are of type (IV);
(3;2,2,2,1,1,1) is of type (III); (1;2,2,2,1,1,1,1) is of type (V);
and (1;3,2,2,1,1,1) is of type (VI). The other eight are of type (I),
with pi_1 the pair, of value 2 for (1;2,2,2,2,1,1) and
(5;2,2,2,1,1), of value 6 for (1;3,3,1,1,1,1) and (3;3,3,1,1,1),
and of value 4 in the other four cases.

In each case every coefficient of Lambda in powers of eta-23 is
strictly positive. Its degree is 54 or 150 in type (II), according
as e = 3 or e = 5; 26, 38, 63 or 81 in type (I), according as
e = 4, 5, 6 or 7; 81 in type (III); 234 in type (IV); 102 in
type (V); and 160 in type (VI). The exceptional resultant in type
(III) has degree 7 and also only positive coefficients in powers
of eta-23. In each of the six zero branches of type (IV), the
remaining numerators of M_3 and M_4 have gcd 1. In type (V) the
two resultants before taking their gcd have degrees 165 and 198;
in type (VI) they have degrees 946 and 1322, and the latter itself
also has only positive coefficients in powers of eta-23.
These computations use exact integer polynomial arithmetic,
Newton identities, pseudo-division, resultants and gcds, with no
interpolation or numerical root tests. They exclude all 29 patterns
for every real n >= 1. Hence d >= 23, and P = n+d/2 >= 25/2.
